messages.author: bf88c5bfbffaf252
messages.subject: package install/loading order
parts:
Hi,

I was wondering is there a specified/best practice order that should be adhered to with regard to installing and loading packages, both cran and custom, and also RHadoop packages when using the mapreduce function?

should they be installed at the same time that rmr2 is installed or can in be done afterwards/before?

can it even be left as late as once ssh'ing into the jobtracker node, and in an R environment?

could it be part of the the function that is being called in which it also calls for the libraries to be installed/loaded if not already loaded?

also with regard to data that the function calls, the main input obviously needs to be converted using the to.dfs function, but what about other objects of data that it might refer to? how is that dealt with? i.e. if a map reduce calls two or more objects...do they need to all be converted using to.dfs? and how would each object be incorporated into the mapreduce function?

thanks

HLM

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#449] package install/loading order
parts:
On Mon, Dec 10, 2012 at 12:28 AM, Hideyoshi Maeda <hideyos...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi,

I was wondering is there a specified/best practice order that should be adhered to with regard to installing and loading packages, both cran and custom, and also RHadoop packages when using the mapreduce function?
Not that I am aware of.
should they be installed at the same time that rmr2 is installed or can in be done afterwards/before?
Besides rmr2 dependendcies, they can be installed afterwards.
can it even be left as late as once ssh'ing into the jobtracker node, and in an R environment?
Since you need to install, in the general case, on all nodes, ssh is not a very scalable way of doing it.
could it be part of the the function that is being called in which it also calls for the libraries to be installed/loaded if not already loaded?

Loading is automatic. that is if you write

library(MASS)

mapreduce(input, map = function(k,v) rlm ...

rlm will be available to the map function as long as MASS was installed on the cluster. We have some development going on to weaken the latter requirement.
also with regard to data that the function calls, the main input obviously needs to be converted using the to.dfs function,

To.dfs is only to create examples, debugging, learning etc. It can not create in a scalable way the amounts of data Hadoop exists to process. So typically the input of a mapreduce call is an HDFS file that was created by some other mean, for instance another mapreduce job. rmr offers the ability to read a number of formats or to define your own format.

but what about other objects of data that it might refer to? how is that dealt with? i.e. if a map reduce calls two or more objects...do they need to all be converted using to.dfs? and how would each object be incorporated into the mapreduce function?

If they are in memory  they can simply be referred to

y = 1

mapreduce(input, function(k,x) x + y)

just works.


If they are too large for this approach, you can give mapreduce multiple inputs


mapreduce(c(input1, input2), ...


Since the two inputs are merged in an arbitrary order, you may want to consider the function equijoin, which uses this approach to implement a limited version of a relational  join.


Antonio

 

thanks

HLM

if for example you wanted to apply a function on an xts object over time using evenly spaced intervals, say for example the last 10 days standard deviation every day (kinda like using a moving window), using the hadoop cluster method, what would be the best Rhadoop/rmr2 way of doing this? (p.s. i know that there are built in functions that already do this example...but i just wanted to use it as an illustrative example, so that instead of standard deviation i could use my own function.) the below is the way I would have done it but perhaps you can come up with a better example especially if to.dfs is not advisable to use. Below is an example of what I would try...

# First generate 10000 days of random univariate data as an xts object
require(xts)
n <- 10000
y <- xts(rnorm(n,0.001, 0.003), order.by=(Sys.Date()-(1:n)))

# a nieve method to apply the standard deviation function across the last 10 days using mapreduce and to.dfs and from.dfs

Looking for a more efficient method of doing this within the mapreduce framework

window.length <- 10

require(rmr2)
sd.vals <- values(
from.dfs(
mapreduce(
input=scatter(
to.dfs(
c(1:(n-window.length))
)),
map=function(k,v){
keyval(k,lapply(X=v, function(x){
sd(
as.numeric(
y[c(x:(x+(window.length-1)))]
))})),

sd.xts.vals <- xts(c(rep(NA,(window.length-1)),sd.vals), order.by=index(y))

note that the object y is being referred to even though it is is not being converted into an dfs format, and is only in memory in the jobtracker node...not any of the other data nodes....(would this be a problem? and if not as suggested below...how does that data get transfered to all data nodes?)

but what about other objects of data that it might refer to? how is that dealt with? i.e. if a map reduce calls two or more objects...do they need to all be converted using to.dfs? and how would each object be incorporated into the mapreduce function?

If they are in memory  they can simply be referred to

y = 1

just works.


If they are too large for this approach, you can give mapreduce multiple inputs


mapreduce(c(input1, input2), ...


Since the two inputs are merged in an arbitrary order, you may want to consider the function equijoin, which uses this approach to implement a limited version of a relational  join.


Antonio

My apologies, I thought this was the real deal. At 3-10 minutes you can run into timeout issues. Hadoop thinks a node is dead if it doesn't collect any output in that time frame. input=scatter(
to.dfs(

If they are in memory  they can simply be referred to

y = 1

mapreduce(input, function(k,x) x + y)

just works.


If they are too large for this approach, you can give mapreduce multiple inputs


mapreduce(c(input1, input2), ...


Since the two inputs are merged in an arbitrary order, you may want to consider the function equijoin, which uses this approach to implement a limited version of a relational  join.
